report.executive_summary: Autonomous threat hunt completed. Multiple ATT&CK techniques confirmed.

findings.title: Brute Force Attack on Administrator Account
findings.description: Detected 15 failed authentication attempts targeting the Administrator account from source IP 192.168.1.105 over a 4-minute window (02:30:03-02:34:27). All attempts used LogonType 3 (network logon) with reason "Unknown user name or bad password". This pattern is consistent with a credential brute force attack. Notably, one successful logon (Event ID 4624) occurred at 02:36:44 from the same source IP, indicating the brute force was ultimately successful.
evidence: Multiple failed logons for Administrator account

findings.title: Credential Dumping via LSASS Process Manipulation
findings.description: Detected credential dumping activity targeting LSASS process. PowerShell commands enumerated the LSASS process at 02:46:20. A Sysmon remote process access event (ID 10) at 02:49:11 shows PowerShell accessing LSASS with GrantedAccess 0x1010. Subsequently, procdump.exe was executed at 02:49:27 with command "procdump.exe -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp" to dump LSASS memory. This is a classic credential dumping attack pattern used to extract cached credentials.
evidence: Sysmon Event 10 remote process access to LSASS at 02:49:11

findings.title: PowerShell Command Execution for Reconnaissance
findings.description: Detected extensive use of PowerShell for system reconnaissance and malicious command execution. Between 02:42:02 and 02:56:28, multiple reconnaissance commands were executed via PowerShell including: hostname (02:42:44), systeminfo (02:44:40), whoami /all (02:45:22), ipconfig /all (02:45:26), and net user (02:46:13). Additionally, a suspicious PowerShell command at 02:42:42 references "C:\\AtomicRedTeam\\invoke-atomicredteam" indicating use of Atomic Red Team testing framework, suggesting this may be simulated attack testing or actual attacker using known techniques.

findings.title: Lateral Movement via SMB/Named Pipes
findings.description: Detected lateral movement attempts to multiple systems via SMB. A command at 03:01:45 executed "net use \\\\192.168.1.110\\C$ /user:Administrator Lab123!" attempting to mount the C$ administrative share on 192.168.1.110 using the compromised Administrator credentials. Network events show SMB connections (port 445) to multiple targets: 192.168.1.115 at 03:01:37 and 192.168.1.110 at 03:03:47. This demonstrates post-compromise lateral movement to other systems in the network.
evidence: net use command to 192.168.1.110 C$ share at 03:01:45
Sysmon Event 3 network connection to 192.168.1.115:445 at 03:01:37
Sysmon Event 3 network connection to 192.168.1.110:445 at 03:03:47

findings.title: Defense Evasion - Windows Defender and Security Disabling
findings.description: Detected multiple attempts to disable Windows Defender protections. PowerShell commands at 02:44:54 and 02:55:58 executed "Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true" and "Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $true" respectively. Additionally, a registry modification at 02:56:28 disabled AntiSpyware via HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\DisableAntiSpyware. These actions were taken to evade antivirus detection during malicious activities.
evidence: Set-MpPreference with DisableRealtimeMonitoring and DisableBehaviorMonitoring at 02:55:58

findings.title: Persistence via Scheduled Task and Registry Run Key
findings.description: Detected persistence mechanisms deployed following successful compromise. A scheduled task was created at 02:53:15 named "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsUpdate\\UpdateCheck" containing PowerShell command with hidden execution (-NoP -W Hidden -c IEX) suggesting execution of downloaded payload. Additionally, a registry modification at 03:06:20 created a Run key at HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\WindowsUpdate pointing to C:\\Users\\Administrator\\AppData\\. This combination of scheduled task and Run key persistence ensures the compromised system maintains backdoor access even after reboot.
evidence: Scheduled task UpdateCheck with PowerShell -NoP -W Hidden at 02:53:15
Registry Run key WindowsUpdate at 03:06:20 pointing to C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\

findings.title: Log Clearing/Evidence Destruction
findings.description: Detected Security Event Log clearing at 03:15:04 (Event ID 1102). The audit log was cleared by the Administrator user post-compromise, likely to remove evidence of the brute force attacks and subsequent malicious activities. This occurred at the end of the attack sequence (02:30-03:15), consistent with typical attacker behavior to cover tracks.
evidence: Event ID 1102 at 03:15:04 - audit log cleared by Administrator
